future_contributions.gap: Scalable data collection for RF fingerprinting
future_contributions.proposed_contribution: Crowdsourced RF signal aggregation framework with device-agnostic data collection
future_contributions.technical_approach: Develop a decentralized data aggregation system leveraging consumer-grade devices (smartphones, IoT sensors) to collect RF signals. Use federated learning for privacy-preserving model training while maintaining dataset diversity.
future_contributions.expected_impact: Enables large-scale, cost-effective RF fingerprinting without specialized hardware, accelerating real-world deployment and improving generalization across device populations.
future_contributions.implementation_feasibility: Feasible via existing mobile device APIs and edge computing infrastructure; requires incentive mechanisms for user participation.

future_contributions.proposed_contribution: Privacy-preserving cross-receiver adaptation using meta-learning with synthetic data augmentation
future_contributions.technical_approach: Train a meta-learner on synthetic RF signal variations generated via domain randomization. Use task-specific prompts to adapt models to new receivers without access to source data.
future_contributions.expected_impact: Significantly improves adaptation performance while maintaining data privacy, enabling deployment across heterogeneous hardware ecosystems.
future_contributions.implementation_feasibility: Feasible with existing synthetic data generation techniques and meta-learning frameworks; requires validation on cross-receiver benchmarks.

future_contributions.gap: Robustness against spoofing in large device populations
future_contributions.proposed_contribution: Hybrid signal-entropy analysis with device-specific behavioral fingerprinting
future_contributions.technical_approach: Combine RF signal analysis with device-specific behavioral patterns (e.g., transmission timing, power fluctuations). Use entropy-based anomaly detection to identify spoofed devices in large-scale networks.
future_contributions.expected_impact: Enhances spoofing resistance in dense device environments, critical for secure IoT and cognitive radio networks.
future_contributions.implementation_feasibility: Feasible via existing signal processing techniques; requires extensive validation on spoofed device datasets.

future_contributions.gap: Handling limited labeled data in SEI
future_contributions.proposed_contribution: Contrastive self-supervised pretraining with synthetic signal augmentation
future_contributions.technical_approach: Generate synthetic emitter signals with controlled parameter variations. Use contrastive learning to learn invariant features, then fine-tune with limited labeled data using virtual adversarial training.
future_contributions.expected_impact: Reduces reliance on labeled data while maintaining performance, critical for real-world SEI applications with sparse annotations.
future_contributions.implementation_feasibility: Feasible with existing signal synthesis tools and contrastive learning frameworks; requires validation on satellite navigation datasets.

future_contributions.proposed_contribution: Adversarial training with frequency-domain perturbation injection
future_contributions.technical_approach: Integrate adversarial examples generated in the frequency domain (via FFT-based perturbations) into the training pipeline. Use gradient masking techniques to prevent adversarial signal detection.
future_contributions.expected_impact: Enhances security against targeted attacks in cognitive radio networks, protecting against primary user emulation threats.
future_contributions.implementation_feasibility: Feasible with existing adversarial training methodologies; requires specialized signal processing for frequency-domain perturbations.

future_contributions.proposed_contribution: Consistency-regularized scribble-supervised segmentation with uncertainty-aware sampling
future_contributions.technical_approach: Implement a dual-branch network: one for scribble-aware segmentation and another for uncertainty estimation. Use consistency loss between branches to enforce robustness against sparse/ambiguous annotations.
future_contributions.expected_impact: Improves segmentation reliability under inconsistent scribble annotations, critical for low-resource semantic segmentation tasks.
future_contributions.implementation_feasibility: Feasible with existing scribble datasets and consistency regularization techniques; requires validation on annotation variability benchmarks.
